messages.subject: variational inference
parts:
hi, i was reading the hoffman et. al. paper on stochastic variational inference (thanks to a comment by Bob on Andrew's blog).  i've read some postings by Andrew and Bob about the incorporation of variational inference into Stan, at some point.  do you have a rough idea for when and will it employ the natural / riemannian gradient based on your work with RMHMC?  will it go further and employ data sub-sampling stochastic variational inference approach?? this would be a game changer for accessible software for estimating bayesian formulations with "big data".  

thanks for your work and support.

terrance

--
Thank you, Terrance Savitsky

> hi, i was reading the hoffman et. al. paper on stochastic variational inference (thanks to a comment by Bob on Andrew's
> blog). i've read some postings by Andrew and Bob about the incorporation of variational inference into Stan, at some
> point. do you have a rough idea for when and will it employ the natural / riemannian gradient based on your work with
> RMHMC? will it go further and employ data sub-sampling stochastic variational inference approach?? this would be a game
> changer for accessible software for estimating bayesian formulations with "big data".
>
> thanks for your work and support.

The plan is to build both batch and stochastic variational
that's general enough to handle non-conjugate models. There may
also be special structure for hierarchical models.

Prototypes are already working for hierarchical models.

The details are still under investigation by Michael Betancourt
and collaborators. Michael's also leading the coding.

We don't really have timelines, but I expect we'll see it
all tied up in a bow in the next year.

- Bob
